title: Sixteen Teams. Five Weeks. And India Open Against Pakistan on Sunday. The Women's T20 World Cup Starts Today.
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's India face the toughest group draw — alongside Australia and South Africa — as the ICC Women's T20 World Cup begins in England.
body:
The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 begins today in England, and for Indian cricket fans, the draw could not be more dramatic: Harmanpreet Kaur's squad opens against Pakistan at Edgbaston on Sunday — a match that will be watched by millions across the diaspora.

The Tournament at a Glance

Sixteen teams are split into two groups. The tournament runs from June 12 to July 5, with matches played across England's most storied cricket grounds — Edgbaston, The Oval, Lord's, and Cardiff's Sophia Gardens.

India are in Group 1 alongside Australia, South Africa, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and the Netherlands. Only two teams from each group qualify for the semi-finals, and with Australia and South Africa also in their pool, India face what is arguably the tougher half of the draw.

Group 2 features hosts England, New Zealand (the defending champions), West Indies, Ireland, Sri Lanka, and Scotland.

Today's opening match sees hosts England take on Sri Lanka at Edgbaston at 6:30 PM BST (1:00 PM ET / 10:00 AM PDT).

India's Squad and Key Players

Captain Harmanpreet Kaur, 37, enters what could be her final major ICC tournament. Her recent T20 form has been exceptional — she was described by The Times as "one of the world's most elegant, skilful and classy batters" in their tournament preview. She is on the verge of breaking the all-time appearance record for India in women's T20 internationals.

Smriti Mandhana provides the firepower at the top, while Shafali Verma — who impressed with bat and ball in the warm-up loss to England — adds explosive energy as both opener and off-spin option. Richa Ghosh proved her big-match temperament with a blazing 68 off 36 balls in that same warm-up, nearly pulling off an improbable chase of 172.

The bowling attack is built around Renuka Singh's pace and Shreyanka Patil's off-spin, with the left-arm variety of Radha Yadav and the all-round presence of Deepti Sharma providing depth. Patil was outstanding in the warm-up games, taking six wickets across two matches.

India's full squad: Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh, Shree Charani, Yastika Bhatia, Nandani Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Renuka Singh, Kranti Gaud, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav.

India's Path Through the Group

India's schedule is demanding. After the Pakistan opener on June 14, they face the Netherlands on June 17, South Africa on June 21, Bangladesh on June 25, and Australia on June 28 — with the semi-finals on July 1 and the final on July 5.

The Australia and South Africa matches will likely decide who advances. South Africa, runners-up in three consecutive ICC finals, have brought back veteran fast bowler Shabnim Ismail from retirement and are led by the tactically sharp Laura Wolvaardt. Australia, meanwhile, are captained by Sophie Molineux after Alyssa Healy's retirement and have the peerless Ellyse Perry still anchoring their lineup at 35.

The Warm-Up Warning

India's narrow five-run loss to England in the warm-up at Cardiff was both encouraging and cautionary. Harmanpreet's decision to field first backfired as England piled up 171/6, with Amy Jones (64 off 45) and Nat Sciver-Brunt (57 off 45) sharing a 70-run partnership. Richa Ghosh's remarkable 68 off 36 nearly rescued the chase, but India were bowled out for 166 in 19.5 overs.

The message was clear: India have the batting to chase any total, but their bowling must be sharper in the tournament proper.

How NRIs Can Watch

In the United States, the tournament streams on Willow TV. In the UK, Sky Sports carries all matches, with the opening game and the final also available free-to-air on Sky Mix and Sky Sports YouTube. In India, JioHotstar has the broadcast rights.

For NRIs in the UK, this is the rare chance to attend a Women's World Cup in person. Tickets for the India-Pakistan match at Edgbaston on Sunday are still available through the ICC website.
